decisions.reason: Both render 수면 위로 equally naturally; 'across the surface' is as idiomatic as 'on the surface.' No meaningful gain.
BASE preserves the source's clause order (lift mouth → dimples) and the image 씻은 듯이 ('as if washed away'); SOL drops that image.
'Hurled' matches the force of 내던지다 better than 'threw,' which weakens the action.
BASE adds 'thought this was a good thing' (unsupported); SOL renders 만들 생각을 하다니 as 'would make something like this' more faithfully.
Both faithful for 쉬지 않고 욕설을 퍼부으며; equally vivid, no net improvement.
These recalled 주의 사항 cautions are not System panels; labeling them 'Warning' complies with the rule against framing non-System material as System.
Dropping the redundant 'genre' yields natural English; 장르 adds nothing over 'martial-arts' here.
Both faithfully render 밖에서 구조해 주기를 and the death-caution; no meaningful difference.
BASE preserves the Korean's emphasis by leading with the quoted clause (…라는 말은), matching source word order.
'answer I'd deduced' tracks 유추해 낸 답; 'reached that conclusion' is fine but loses 'answer' with no offsetting gain.
'Completing Tutorial—Stage 1' replaces a stiff nominal ('The completion of') with direct verbal phrasing, same meaning.
Both natural for 사흘간의 고민; 'thinking' and 'thought' are equivalent here.
활동해야 한다 means 'must operate/be active'; BASE's 'stay' drifts, SOL's 'operate' is more faithful.
BASE's 'exactly the right place' tracks 딱 알맞은; SOL's 'just the place' is idiomatic but no better.
Both render 데려다줄 마차 naturally; indistinguishable quality.
SOL preserves 말 한마디 ('didn't say a word'), which BASE paraphrases away as 'never tried to make conversation.'
Both faithful; SOL's reordering is stylistic and adds no clarity gain.
'the only power unique to you' tracks 당신만이 가진 유일한 힘 more closely than 'your only unique power'; capitalized objective matches System notice style.
BASE drops 어쩌면 ('maybe') and adds 'really'; SOL keeps the source's uncertainty.
SOL renders 과거 가뭄에 콩 나듯 as the idiom 'once in a blue moon' without BASE's redundant 'in the past.'
BASE's 'from a prestigious Murim family' matches 출신; 'member of' paraphrases without gain.
특이 사항 is 'special notes'; BASE preserves 특이, SOL flattens to 'the notes.'
Both adequately render 괜히 가문의 수치가 아니다 and the wastrel description; no meaningful gain.
원하는 능력치 rendered equally well; 'whichever' adds no fidelity or notable clarity.
'treat as' is more standard than 'treat like'; equal faithfulness.
BASE's appositive construction ('qi—mana or aura—that Hunters used') tracks 마나, 오러 같은 기 more closely than SOL's rephrasing.
Em-dash vs comma is purely punctuation; both faithful and equal.
Both render 제외하다; 'exclude' and 'rule out' are equivalent here.
Both render 어떤 것들이 필요한지; 'what was needed' and 'what it took' are equal.
Korean uses 회피 ('evasion'), not 민첩; SOL's 'evasiveness' is faithful, while BASE substitutes the stat name 'Agility' into prose.
SOL's staccato verbs match the Korean's terse present-tense 잇는다/뭉치고/풀어낸다, and 'unseen depths' preserves 몸속 깊은 곳.
'swept through my body' matches 몸을 휩쓸었다; dropping 'body' is a stylistic wash, not an improvement.
경악했다 is 'was stunned/shocked'; SOL's 'froze' adds a physical beat the source doesn't give.
SOL's 'Not from…, but because…' matches the Korean's 아니다…때문이었다 causal structure and keeps 느꼈던/떠올랐다.
BASE preserves the source's deliberate split and dangling object ('How could I forget? That day, seven years ago.'); SOL flattens it.
BASE keeps the appositive fragment 'The chosen 0.1 percent.' matching 선택받은 0.1%; SOL's 'One of' alters the beat.
환희 is 'exhilaration/rapture'; SOL preserves 느꼈던 ('felt') and 지금 ('now'), while BASE's 'how happy' softens.
SOL's 'parched lips' captures 바짝 마른 better than BASE's 'already dry.'
BASE preserves 우선 ('for now'), which SOL omits.
Source 구결을 잊은 is singular and glossary term is 'formula'; SOL's plural 'formulas' violates the term and source number.
'widened my eyes' is the more idiomatic rendering of 눈을 부릅뜨고 than 'opened my eyes wide.'
BASE preserves the deliberate odd repetition 'and three' (그리고 셋); SOL replaces the joke with 'and that was it.'
가진 스킬 rendered naturally as 'had'; 'possessed' is stiffer with no gain.
SOL preserves 많이 ('more'); BASE drops it, losing the source's 'learn plenty later.'
Source 단어 is singular ('one word'); SOL's 'two terms' adds specificity not in the Korean.
핏줄 = blood vessels; SOL corrects BASE's narrower 'veins.'
Comma vs 'and' in the parallel list is trivial; both faithful.
SOL conveys the idiom 고기도 먹어 본 놈이 잘 먹지 (experience helps) better than BASE's 'only handle what you've tried.'
SOL's word order mirrors 몸 깊은 곳에서 뼈가 뒤틀리는 more directly and reads naturally.
SOL preserves 자리에는 ('all that remained was…') and 헐떡이는 숨소리 ('ragged breathing'), which BASE restructures away.
BASE keeps 앞뒤 ('front and back') and 단단 ('hardened'); SOL narrows to 'chest and back' and adds 'covered.'
느낄 수 없었던 is 'couldn't sense'; BASE preserves the perception framing, while SOL's 'hadn't been there' shifts to existence.
Both render 끝이 어딘지 adequately; 'endpoint' and 'limit' are equal here.
BASE's comma form matches the Korean's '더, 더, 더' structure; SOL's periods change the punctuation without clear gain.
BASE's 'found myself' captures 어느새…발견했다; SOL's 'suddenly I was dressed' loses that beat. Roughly equal otherwise.
BASE's 'was wearing… instead of' matches 신었다; SOL's 'had replaced' personifies with no gain.
BASE includes both 벗겨진 ('I'd taken off') and 손 ('from my hands'); SOL drops 'taken off.'
Both render 어떻게 쓰느냐에 따라 전투에 응용할 수도; word-order swap yields no meaningful improvement.
세우다 = build/put up; SOL's 'buy a whole building' is a mistranslation.
BASE's terse 'be careful when handling it' suits the System description register; SOL's 'exercise caution' is stiffer.
Both render 창자루 ('spear shaft') naturally; no meaningful difference.
배움에는 결과가 있어야 is 'learning must have results'; SOL's 'produce results' tracks 결과, whereas BASE's 'put into practice' substitutes a different idea.
